messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 -> SEA-POP packet-loss alert. Aggregate egress packet loss crossing 5% for prefix 203.0.113.0/24; affected edge nodes: edge-sea-01, edge-sea-02. Link: https://ops.internal/incidents/1991234567 :rotating_light:

amelia: seeing a big jump in TCP retransmits and client 502/504s from the SEA POP. Started ~03:42 UTC, persists. Quick metrics: p50->p95 latency +120ms, 5xx rate up ~3% absolute (from 0.2%). Clients mostly west-coast retail and a couple gaming partners.

mike_net: running quick checks on the colo uplinks and AS paths. Confirmed elevated interface drops on uplink1 (tx errors) on edge-sea-01. Suspect last-mile ISP issue or a flapping peering.

mike_net: commands executed:
```
# check neighbor and counters
show interfaces eth1
show bgp neighbors 198.51.100.1 | include 198.51.100.1
ping 198.51.100.5 size 1400 count 50
tcpdump -i eth1 'tcp and (dst port 443)' -c 100 -w /tmp/sea-443.pcap
```

jordan_sre: @mike_net thanks. If uplink looks flaky, let's steer traffic away from SEA while we investigate. Plan: apply temporary traffic steering to prefer us-west1 and increase healthcheck strictness on SEA prefixes.

sara_support: I'm drafting a customer note for affected tenants. Minimal impact so far but spikes in errors for a subset of API calls. I'll include mitigation steps and ETA to next update in 30m.

deploy-bot: Applied traffic-steering policy ts-policy-1991234567 -> prefer-us-west1 for prefix 203.0.113.0/24 (policy id p-77).

amelia: after steering, we're seeing gradual drop in client-side errors for routed traffic, but some sessions still hit SEA due to cached BGP paths. p95 latency is trending down for new flows.

mike_net: asked colo NOC to check fiber pair and re-provision port. They're seeing some CRC and FCS errors on the fiber, opened ticket CORD-4521. Vendor is switching to alternate fiber path now.

tim_prod: any known deploys or config changes around SEA in last hour? I don't see any from infra pipelines.

infra-bot: No infra deploys targeting edge-sea in the last 6 hours.

jordan_sre: Good. Current mitigation status: 1) traffic-steering applied (reduces exposure), 2) colo vendor working hardware path, 3) healthcheck strictness increased so unhealthy backends are pulled faster. Next: if vendor can't stabilize within 30m, we'll shift more capacity to us-west1 and notify top-10 customers directly.

david_ops: I'm on my way to join the bridge in 10. Handoff at T+25. Leaving notes: packet loss observed on uplink1, vendor ticket CORD-4521, steering policy p-77 active, partial recovery for new flows.

sara_support: Notified customers: AcmeRetail, StreamCo, GameHub (list withheld). Sent interim update w/ suggested client retry guidance and mitigation. No paid SLA breaches yet but warning threshold approaching for two tenants.

mike_net: vendor confirmed fiber switch complete, CRC errors falling. Still seeing ~1% loss on short bursts. Running path MTU tests and jumbo frame checks.

jordan_sre: Re-checking global edge metrics — other POPs stable. SEA shows condensed spikes; could be last-mile ISP BGP flap. If vendor confirms, our permanent fix is to add passive health probes and lower BGP local-pref for flaky peer until vendor permanently repairs.

deploy-bot: Route announcement update: withdrew 203.0.113.128/25 from SEA edges for 30m.

amelia: After withdrawal, error rate returned almost to baseline for the affected customers. Some long-lived TCP sessions still seeing issues until re-establish.

david_ops: Taking over on-call. Summary for next oncall: root cause likely last-mile fiber/peer instability at SEA colo causing transient packet loss; vendor ticket CORD-4521; steering policy p-77 applied; withdrawal of .128/25 in effect; follow vendor remediation and validate with 10-minute histograms. Escalation if packet loss >0.5% persists longer than 45m.

sara_support: I'll follow up with the customers we notified and provide the handoff summary to support rotations.

jordan_sre: Create a quick post-incident checklist:
- confirm vendor repaired fiber and zero CRCs for 1 hour
- re-announce withdrawn prefix and monitor for recurrence
- add runbook step to automate temporary route withdrawal + steering for similar events
- review BGP communities and set auto-preference for known flaky peers

infra-bot: Running automated regression check against canary traffic in SEA. No config regressions detected.

mike_net: final note — consider adding a passive synthetic that pings behind the edge routers from 3 vantage points in the metro to detect pre-failure jitter.

jordan_sre: Agreed. I'll open a ticket to add that probe and assign to netops.

sara_support: Next customer update will go out in 20m after vendor confirms repair or we re-announce the prefix.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). Severity remains P2 until prefix is re-announced and stable for 60 minutes. Incident link: https://ops.internal/incidents/1991234567

jordan_sre: Handoff complete to @david_ops. If anything flares, page the on-call rotation. Otherwise we'll convert to postmortem doc once ticket CORD-4521 is closed. :white_check_mark:
